alternatives.root_cause: A cache/memory leak in recommendation caused it to fan out far more product-catalog calls, saturating the catalog
alternatives.why_not: recommendation is not a dependency of checkout, yet checkout alerted too - the shared factor across all alerting callers is product-catalog itself, not recommendation.

alternatives.root_cause: A flagd-driven flag flipped a failing/slow code path that product-catalog or its callers execute
alternatives.why_not: product-catalog has no edge to flagd here, and the flagd-dependent services that did not alert (ad, cart, product-reviews, fraud-detection) argue against a flag-store-wide change.

verdict.summary: product-catalog became slow under its own resource pressure (CPU/thread/connection saturation), and every caller that waits on it inherited the latency
verdict.reasoning: The alerting set is exactly product-catalog plus everything that sits upstream of it: frontend, recommendation and checkout all call product-catalog directly, frontend-proxy fronts frontend, and load-generator is the synthetic client at the top. Services that do not depend on product-catalog (ad, cart, currency, payment, shipping, email, product-reviews) are only in the blast radius by graph traversal, not alerting. That makes product-catalog the deepest alerting node and the common ancestor of all the others. product-catalog has no outgoing edges in this graph, so it cannot have inherited the latency from a downstream call - the slowness originates inside it. The symptom is latency rather than hard errors, which fits saturation (CPU burn, exhausted worker pool or connection pool) rather than a crash-looping artifact or a full disk, both of which would surface as refusals rather than slow successes.
